translationRepairs: Miao Jingqing; Pei Mian; Pei Zunqing; Zi Xiang; Zi Xiang's son Yin; Yin's son Shu.
Miao Jingqing; Pei Mian; Pei Zunqing; his son Xiang; Xiang's son Yin; Yin's son Shu.
s0001 子向 is kinship plus given name Xiang after 裴遵慶, not a personal name Zi Xiang; 向子寅 and 寅子樞 continue the same father–son chain.
Miao Jingqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, Zi Xiang, Zi Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu.
Miao Jingqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, son Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu.
Same roster: 子向 is 'son Xiang', not Zi Xiang; the literal replacement restores the kinship parsing.
His grandfather Kui was a man of lofty character who did not take office; posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
His grandfather Kui was a man of lofty character who did not take office; posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.
s0004 追贈禮部尚書 is a posthumous honorary office grant; 追贈 is not territorial enfeoffment (封).

His father Daiyi had served as assistant magistrate of Longmen county in Jiang prefecture and died young; on account of Jingqing's honors he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

His father Daishu had served as assistant magistrate of Longmen county in Jiang prefecture and died young; on account of Jingqing's honors he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
s0005 父殆庶 reads Daishu (殆庶), not Daiyi; the replacement restores the correct given name.
His father Daiyi reached the post of Assistant Magistrate of Longmen in Jiang prefecture, died young, and through Jingqing was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
His father Daishu reached the post of Assistant Magistrate of Longmen in Jiang prefecture, died young, and through Jingqing was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
Same unit: 殆庶 is Daishu, and 贈太子少保 is a posthumous honor, not an enfeoffment.
He was first appointed magistrate of Xiuwu county in Huai prefecture, later served as magistrate of Fengxian, and was eventually demoted to registrar of Xu prefecture after a series of entanglements.

He was first appointed county defender of Xiuwu in Huai prefecture, later served as county defender of Fengxian, and was eventually demoted to registrar of Xu prefecture after a series of entanglements.
s0007 縣尉 is the county defender/commandant; magistrate would be 令/長.
At first he was appointed Magistrate of Xiuwu in Huai prefecture, served as Magistrate of Fengxian, and through accumulated offenses was demoted to Registrar of Xu prefecture.
At first he was appointed County Defender of Xiuwu in Huai prefecture, served as County Defender of Fengxian, and through accumulated offenses was demoted to Registrar of Xu prefecture.
Same unit: 縣尉 is County Defender, not Magistrate; the literal replacement matches the office.
When his term ended he entered the regular reassignment process, received a top evaluation, and was appointed magistrate of Wannian county.
When his term ended he entered the regular reassignment process, received a top evaluation, and was appointed county defender of Wannian county.
s0008 萬年縣尉 is county defender, not county magistrate.
When his term expired he followed the regular transfer, was judged in the upper grade, and was appointed Magistrate of Wannian.
When his term expired he followed the regular transfer, was judged in the upper grade, and was appointed County Defender of Wannian.
Same unit: 縣尉 must not be rendered Magistrate.
Pei Mian was a man of Hedong and was a leading clan of Hedong.
Pei Mian was a man of Hedong and belonged to a leading clan of Hedong.
s0081 為河東冠族 means he belonged to Hedong's foremost clan; saying he 'was a leading clan' misidentifies the person as the clan.
Early in the Tianbao era he entered office through hereditary privilege and was twice promoted to magistrate of Weinan, where he won a reputation for administrative skill.
Early in the Tianbao era he entered office through hereditary privilege and was twice promoted to county lieutenant of Weinan, where he won a reputation for administrative skill.
s0082 渭南縣尉 is a county lieutenant/defender (尉), not the county magistrate (令).
At the beginning of Tianbao, through hereditary privilege he was twice promoted to Magistrate of Weinan and became known for the way of clerical administration.
At the beginning of Tianbao, through hereditary privilege he was twice promoted to Lieutenant of Weinan County and became known for the way of clerical administration.
Same unit: 縣尉 is not Magistrate; Lieutenant of Weinan County restores the office.
Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he kept silent and they did not dare harm him.
Jingqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he kept silent and they did not dare harm him.
s0217 晉卿 is the same person earlier rendered Jingqing; shifting to Jinqing mid-chapter invents an unwarranted alternate romanization.
When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jinqing was made grand guardian, relieved of government, and again ordered to retire with that title.
When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jingqing was made grand guardian, relieved of government, and again ordered to retire with that title.
s0218 晉卿 must stay Jingqing with the chapter's established English; the original 'made' already renders 冊為 as appointment, so changing it to 'invested' is only stylistic.
When the Emperor came from Shaan, Jinqing was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, ceased knowing administration, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.
When the Emperor came from Shaan, Jingqing was invested as Grand Guardian, ceased knowing administration, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.
s0218 冊為太保 is investiture/appointment, not feudal enfeoffment, and the personal name should remain Jingqing.
Earlier, when Jinqing was eastern capital guardian, he had appointed Yuan Zai, an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.
Earlier, when Jingqing was eastern capital guardian, he had appointed Yuan Zai, an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.
s0222 晉卿 is again the same Jingqing; Jinqing is an inconsistent romanization without Chinese warrant.

The Heir Apparent said: 'To pacify the south of the bandits and rebels, welcome the imperial carriage, withdraw to dwell as heir designate, and attend meals at the left and right—would this not be joy!
The Heir Apparent said: 'To pacify the rebel bandits in the south, welcome the imperial carriage, withdraw to dwell as heir designate, and attend meals at his side—would this not be joy!
s0095 南平寇逆 means to pacify the rebels in the south, not 'the south of the bandits'; the replacement restores that sense.
Your primordial constancy reaches the ten thousand states; for more than twenty years deep sorrow has opened the sage—today is exactly the time.
Your steadfast virtue has upheld the myriad states for more than twenty years; it is through deep trial that the sage is revealed—and that moment is today.
s0098 元貞萬國，二十余年，殷憂啟聖，正在今日 pairs long upright stewardship of the myriad states with revelation through deep trial; the original literal jumbles those clauses.

When Suzong ascended the throne, for merit in settling the plan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and relied on for government.

When Suzong ascended the throne, for merit in settling the plan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and made equal-to-chief-minister (tong Zhongshu Menxia pingzhang shi), and relied on for government.
s0102 同中書門下平章事 is a chief-minister designation, not Concurrent Regular Attendant.
Zai had once been magistrate of Xinping. When Wang Hong recruited him into his inspection staff, Mian had often spoken well of him, and Zai felt deep gratitude toward Mian.
Zai had once been county defender of Xinping. When Wang Hong recruited him into his inspection staff, Mian had often spoken well of him, and Zai felt deep gratitude toward Mian.
s0116 新平縣尉 is county defender, not county magistrate (令).
Zai had been Magistrate of Xinping; Wang Hong recruited him within his circuit inspection, and Mian often recommended him—Zai was quite grateful to Mian.
Zai had been County Defender of Xinping; Wang Hong recruited him within his circuit inspection, and Mian often recommended him—Zai was quite grateful to Mian.
Same unit: 縣尉 is County Defender, not Magistrate.
The emperor mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal, and granted funeral gifts of five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain.
The emperor mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously honored him as Grand Marshal, and granted funeral gifts of five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain.
s0126 贈太尉 is a posthumous honorific office, not an enfeoffment.
When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting attendant, right assistant in the Secretariat, and vice minister of personnel.
When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting attendant, right assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and vice minister of personnel.
s0136 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), not the Secretariat (中書).
When Suzong ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Drafting Attendant, Right Assistant in the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
When Suzong ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Drafting Attendant, Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
Same unit: 尚書右丞 is Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, not of the Secretariat.

When a candidate named Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing, spoke insolently and behaved outrageously at the selection bureau, Emperor Daizong ordered Zunqing to have him flogged thirty times at the ministry gate and demoted him to outside registrar of Ji prefecture.

When a candidate named Chen Guan, county lieutenant of Tianxing, spoke insolently and behaved outrageously at the selection bureau, Emperor Daizong ordered Zunqing to have him flogged thirty times at the ministry gate and demoted him to outside registrar of Ji prefecture.
s0145 天興縣尉 is a county lieutenant/defender; magistrate would be 縣令.

At the time the candidate Chen Guan, Magistrate of Tianxing, used insubordinate words in the selection courtyard, arrogant and without propriety; Daizong ordered him handed to Zunqing for thirty lashes at the ministry gate and demoted to Outside Registrar of Ji prefecture.

At the time the candidate Chen Guan, County Lieutenant of Tianxing, used insubordinate words in the selection courtyard, arrogant and without propriety; Daizong ordered him handed to Zunqing for thirty lashes at the ministry gate and demoted to Outside Registrar of Ji prefecture.
Same unit: 縣尉 must not be rendered Magistrate.

When Zunqing first entered as a provincial bureau gentleman he once authored 'Record of Royal Government,' setting forth ancient and modern ritual forms; those of discernment who read it knew he had the capacity of chief minister.

When Zunqing first entered as a capital ministry gentleman he once authored 'Record of Royal Government,' setting forth ancient and modern ritual forms; those of discernment who read it knew he had the capacity of chief minister.
s0149 省郎 means a gentleman of the capital ministries, not a provincial (外官) bureau post.

Guixian forced the county magistrate Lin Bao to press the laborers in building the ramparts. When the work fell behind schedule he was about to execute Lin, and officials and common people fled in terror.

Guixian forced the county lieutenant Lin Bao to press the laborers in building the ramparts. When the work fell behind schedule he was about to execute Lin, and officials and common people fled in terror.
s0153 縣尉林寶 is county lieutenant Lin Bao, not the county magistrate.
Guixian compelled the county magistrate Lin Bao to press laborers for plank construction; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead him, and clerks, people, and commoners fled in panic.
Guixian compelled the county lieutenant Lin Bao to press laborers for plank construction; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead him, and clerks, people, and commoners fled in panic.
Same unit: 縣尉 is county lieutenant/defender, not magistrate.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
s0170 贈太子少保 is a posthumous honorific appointment; 贈 is not enfeoffment (封).
In the Dazhun era Kong Wei was demoted for military failure. Shu was implicated and made right guardian of the heir apparent, then sent out as prefect of She.
In the Dashun era Kong Wei was demoted for military failure. Shu was implicated and made right guardian of the heir apparent, then sent out as prefect of She.
s0180 大順 is the Tang reign Dashun; Dazhun misreads 順.
Before long he was exchanged to Vice Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and made a chief minister (tong pingzhangshi).
s0185 同平章事 denotes chief-minister status, not Regular Attendant of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

When Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized to employ his military officer Zhang Tingfan as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the chief ministers discussed it, and Shu said: 'Tingfan is a meritorious minister—fortunately he may receive a regional command with military commission; what need has he of the Director of Music?

When Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized to employ his military officer Zhang Tingfan as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the chief ministers discussed it, and Shu said: 'Tingfan is a meritorious minister—fortunately he may receive a regional command with military commission; what need has he of the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices?
s0191 樂卿 is a literary epithet for 太常卿 (Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices), not a separate 'Director of Music'.

On the eleventh day of the sixth month, when he reached Hua prefecture on his way into exile, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post and throw his body into the river. He was sixty-five years old.

On the eleventh day of the sixth month, when he reached Hua prefecture on the Yellow River on his way into exile, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post and throw his body into the river. He was sixty-five years old.

s0198 滑州 is the Yellow River Hua, distinct from earlier 華州 in Guanzhong; the proposal correctly flags the ambiguity but inserts Chinese into the English field, so revise to English-only disambiguation.
